Blends the look LUT with the unfiltered image — 100 is the full look, lower values fade it toward the original.
Colour negative: the orange mask is cancelled per channel. Black and white: one exponent for all channels and a neutral result.
Click an unexposed film-base area (the clear rebate). The colour is averaged from the original image, so crop, rotation and zoom do not matter.
Sets the red and blue ratios so the converted scene averages neutral. Needs a picked film base; it will not guess one.
Reference exponent (green). Higher gives more contrast. RawTherapee default 1.5.

By default Tone adjustments apply to every loaded photo. Click to make THIS photo's adjustments independent (e.g. nudge just its exposure), or click again to sync it back to the shared value.
One-click levels and white balance from the image histogram
Warms (or cools) skin/orange tones only — everything else is unaffected. Dial to taste; not a color-accuracy control.
Contrast in the finest source detail band (approximately 1–2 pixels). Zero leaves the image unchanged.
Contrast in the small-detail band (approximately 2–4 source pixels). Zero leaves the image unchanged.
Contrast in the medium-detail band (approximately 4–8 source pixels). Zero leaves the image unchanged.
Contrast in the low-frequency residual around the renderer's working-value midpoint (0.5). Zero leaves the image unchanged.
Click a neutral (grey/white) area to auto-correct white balance

Off: untouched decode. Fast (default): the native Rust-side shadow + chroma-wavelet denoise on linear RAW data, before any tone curve — a few seconds, applies automatically. High: additionally runs a neural (RawNIND UtNet2) denoiser, 25–90s at 24MP — never automatic; press "Denoise now" below, or it runs once at export if selected. Requires reopening this photo (or Denoise now) to take effect. Desktop/RAW only.

RAW opens with only the chroma-noise cleanup applied, so it is ready quickly. Turn this on to also apply shadow noise reduction, false-colour suppression and hue defringe while you edit (reloads this photo, a few seconds longer). Export always applies them, whichever way this is set.

Real-photo review (5 ISO 12800 shots vs DxO PureRAW) found full strength can soften fine hair/fur strands more than DxO does, even though flat-area noise removal is comparable or better — lower this if High is smoothing detail you want to keep. Changing it re-arms Denoise now / re-applies at next export.

Choose the decode-time method for this photo. AHD, VNG and MHC support Bayer sensors. Markesteijn 1-pass and 3-pass support standard X-Trans layouts. An incompatible choice is rejected by the decoder. Requires reopening this photo to take effect. Desktop only.

Capture sharpening — RAW photos default to 40 on load/reset (moved here so it survives Reset independently of the general Adjust sliders).
Source-pixel radius for the sharpening halo. The default 1.0 preserves today's sharpening exactly.
Balances edge-only sharpening at lower values against fine texture at higher values. The default 50 preserves today's sharpening exactly.
Protect smooth areas from sharpening. Hold Alt to preview white sharpened edges and black protected areas.
Sharpen Mask; hold Alt to preview

Bright specular highlights (sunlit water, glints) sometimes show green/magenta demosaic false-color that no amount of Luminance/Color NR fully removes. Since real highlight color is usually near-neutral anyway, this fades Cb/Cr toward zero from mid-tones (~45%) up through highlights — reaches far enough to cover where the fringing actually sits, so it WILL flatten real color in bright areas too at high amounts. Per-photo only, so it never touches other images.

Shows the EFFECTIVE selection in red — shape combined with the luminance and colour-range gates. The Overlay/Isolate modes draw the shape only.

Desktop only: looks up this exact camera+lens+focal-length in a bundled lens-profile database (lensfun) and geometrically corrects distortion automatically on next RAW load. Falls back to the manual sliders below when no profile match exists.

Overrides EXIF auto-detection with a lens you pick directly — for manual/adapted lenses that write no lens EXIF at all. Picking one also turns Auto on.
Focal length in mm — required for distortion correction. Auto-filled for fixed (prime) lenses.
Straightens bowed lines. Positive fixes barrel distortion (lines bow outward), negative fixes pincushion (lines bow inward).
Brightens the corners to counteract lens vignetting.
Corrects red/blue fringing near high-contrast edges, worst in the corners.

Removes purple/green color fringes on high-contrast edges — the local fringing that survives the geometric CA correction above, or that a fast lens makes wide open. Gated on edges, so flat purple or green subjects are left alone.
Swap the picked aspect ratio between portrait and landscape (e.g. 3:2 ↔ 2:3) — the chip list above only lists one orientation each.
Copies this photo's crop/rotate/flip/straighten onto every other loaded photo, overwriting theirs
Finds the dominant horizontal or vertical line and levels it. Says so plainly when there isn't one.
Constrains where Auto level looks for a line — useful when a stronger false line elsewhere in the frame (a wave, a shoreline fragment) keeps outscoring the real horizon.
Clear region — Auto level goes back to searching the whole frame
Corrects converging verticals while preserving perspective spacing.
Corrects horizontal perspective for a wall or facade photographed from one side.
Fine perspective rotation, in tenths of a degree.
Scales the perspective-corrected photo to hide empty frame edges.
Fine-tune the grain clump size on top of the film format (5 = format-accurate).
Dehancer film-format grain: smaller formats are coarser/stronger, 65mm is the finest & weakest.
0 = grain frozen to the screen. 100 = fully independent every frame (can boil at high Amount). Real film sits in between.
Sub-pixel frame-to-frame wobble, the way a projector gate holds film. A little goes a long way — past about 30 it reads as a shaky camera rather than a projector.
Per-frame exposure flicker, the way a projector lamp and shutter never deliver exactly the same light twice.
Random dust specks and the odd hair — mostly light (dust on the negative prints white).
Thin vertical emulsion scratches with a gentle wobble.
A warm light leak flooding in from one edge.
Keeps dark areas (eyes, nostrils, deep shadows) from flooding red. 0 = full film behavior.

Film with no anti-halation backing (remjet) — much stronger, bloomier halos with a yellow→orange→red edge, calibrated to Dehancer's no-remjet look.

Adds or removes fine surface detail (radius-1 high-pass) — positive adds crunchy texture/grain-like detail, negative softens it. Distinct from Clarity's wider midtone-structure move.

Cuts atmospheric haze in the distance — extra contrast/black-point/saturation, but only where the image reads BRIGHT and DESATURATED (a hazy sky or ridge), so foreground color is left alone. Negative values add haze back in.
